newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Feb 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Feb 3.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Monday:

WASHINGTON - Mayor Marion Barry will unveil a $3.3 billion spending plan today that would balance the District's budget in 1998 by cutting millions of dollars from prisons, D.C. General Hospital and job training.
HONG KONG - For U.S. agricultural exporters, banks, insurance companies, brokerage houses and advertising firms, Hong Kong is a key market.
WASHINGTON - Given the choice, Virginia juries are voting for life sentences rather than the death penalty.
WASHINGTON - Critics are asking if President Clinton's nominee for Labor Secretary, Alexis Herman, elevated politics at the White House Office of Public Liaison to a new and more dangerous level.

SUDBURY, ONTARIO - Canada considers hockey its game and a highly regimented system has developed to pick the best players, beginning before puberty, but intense competition also puts teen prospects at risk.
WASHINGTON - Economists, congressional leaders and even university officials are worred that the president's $50 billion proposal to provide new access to higher education is fraught with risks.
